svg.title: Four multi-tenant isolation layers and the assumption each one rests on
svg.desc: Four rows, one per isolation layer. Compute isolation uses hardware-virtualized microVMs such as Firecracker and Kata Containers, or a userspace application kernel such as gVisor, and rests on the hypervisor or sandbox itself not being escapable. Storage isolation uses row-level security, per-tenant schemas, or separate instances, and rests on every query path running as a tenant-scoped role. Cryptographic isolation uses per-tenant key hierarchies and rests on the calling role being scoped to one tenant's key rather than to all of them. Identity isolation uses assume-role sessions tagged with a tenant identifier and rests on resource policies actually reading that tag. A footer states that these layers reduce the blast radius of a tenant boundary failure and do not eliminate escape.
svg.text: Each layer bounds a different failure. None of them is unconditional — the right-hand column is what has to hold.

An untagged or wildcard policy grants the whole

These layers reduce the blast radius of a tenant boundary failure. None of them eliminates escape — assume one layer fails and check what the next still holds.
